issue_request: FHIR-17906 was a Published FHIR-I change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for STU3, asking the conditional update section to distinguish no-match/no-id creation, no-match/id Update as Create behavior, one-match update when no id or matching id is supplied, and one-match rejection when the supplied resource id conflicts with the found resource.
initial_application: The issue was explicitly applied by d69dfafe26d9ad9151c011ef743568a3ab2158fc, which replaced the generic conditional update No matches/One Match bullets in source/http.html with the split no-id, id-provided, matching-id, mismatching-id, and multiple-match outcomes.
additional_context: The current active page is source/http.html, included by publish.ini as http.html. Later finalized same-section issues refined but did not reverse the seed behavior: FHIR-20390 clarified id-provided wording to Resource.id, FHIR-26688 removed the contradictory ignore-id sentence, FHIR-36859 split the no-match/Resource.id case when that id already exists, and FHIR-26358 added response Location guidance. These related issues are already represented on the combined branch. A 2025 Zulip thread questions one-match response-status wording, but no finalized Jira decision was found for that separate concern.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/http.html already says no-match/no Resource.id creates the resource; no-match/Resource.id with no existing id uses Update as Create or rejects if unsupported; no-match/Resource.id with an existing id returns 409 Conflict; one match updates when no Resource.id is supplied or when it matches the found resource; and one-match/mismatching Resource.id returns 400 Bad Request.
